page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a shared-resource virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It provisions 2 shared vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a 2.0 GHz clock speed, paired with 4.0 GB of memory to yield a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor supplies standard AVX, AES, and SHA extensions while lacking AVX-512 instruction sets. This tier contains no bundled local storage, no hardware GPU accelerators, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reflects performance characteristics typical of shared entry-level infrastructure. The server exhibits reasonable single-core throughput, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 1862.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 23.61 GB/sec. However, parallel execution and memory efficiency fall into lower tiers; Geekbench multi-core scores reach 3294.0, while PassMark CPU registers 4191.67. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 12.62 GB/sec for large-block reads and 10.18 GB/sec for writes, which constrains static web serving throughput to 2.15 GB/sec and PassMark database operations to 1356.4.

Given the shared CPU allocation and complete absence of local disk drives, the instance delivers a low resource footprint prioritized for secondary utility. It is best aligned with lightweight decoupled microservices, development and testing environments, asynchronous task runners, and stateless workloads that do not demand sustained compute concurrency or persistent local storage.
